children: Brunei’s trade surplus surged to BND 884.9 million in August 2026 from BND 415.9 million in the same month a year earlier, marking its highest level since April as exports grew much faster than imports.
Exports jumped 58.0% yoy to BND 1.75 billion, the highest since July 2022, driven by strong gains in mineral fuels (61.6%) and chemicals (55.8%).
China was the largest export destination, accounting for 22.9% of total shipments, followed by Australia (22.1%), Singapore (15.3%), and South Korea (9.3%).
Meanwhile, imports rose at a slower pace of 25.2% to BND 870.0 million, led by higher purchases of mineral fuels (37.5%), chemicals (15.7%), and food (11.3%).
Malaysia remained the largest import source, supplying 57.6% of total imports, followed by Vietnam (11.4%), Sweden (5.6%), China (4.7%), and Nigeria (4.5%).
In the first eight months of the year, the trade surplus widened to BND 5.11 billion from BND 3.40 billion a year earlier, as exports increased 35.8% while imports rose 27.2%.

title: Brunei Trade Surplus More than Doubles as Exports Surge
